# Carbon Energy Nexus

> A free daily publication at carbonenergynexus.com on where carbon, energy, water and capital meet: CO2 capture and storage, carbon markets and removals, energy policy, produced water and the water footprint of energy, project finance and research. Each edition sorts news by electrons (power), molecules (fuels), pore space (the subsurface) and water, tracks projects on a seven step ladder from announcement to operation, and says what each story means for investors, regulators, industry and founders. Facts are sourced and dated; stages and outlooks are labeled as our judgment. General information, not investment advice.

## Tools
- [Energy and carbon footprint calculator](https://carbonenergynexus.com/calculator.html): households and companies, EPA and EIA factors, transparent Nexus Score
- [Frameworks](https://carbonenergynexus.com/frameworks.html): how projects, policy and carbon claims are judged

## Today's edition
- [COP31's new draft drops fossil fuel language but keeps a carbon capture goal](https://carbonenergynexus.com/): November 20, 2026. COP31's second draft deal, released Nov 19, removes every direct reference to fossil fuels but keeps a goal of at least 500 million tonnes of carbon capture a year by 2035, still in brackets, and a 35% electrification target.
- [Markets: Canada starts buying durable carbon removal through a standing federal offer](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#money)
- [Water: Jordan launches a $6.6 billion plan to pipe desalinated Red Sea water to Amman](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#world)
- [Projects: New York names 10 nuclear developers as federal reviews speed up](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#nuclear)
- [Projects: A paper mill turbine runs on pure hydrogen, and the cost question follows](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#hydrogen)
- [Water: New Mexico drills for brackish water, and brine disposal goes underground](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#water)
